battle.name: 巴柯巴起義
battle.theater: 不列顛北部泰恩至索爾韋灣防線
battle.brief: 公元132年，不列顛行省北部與威爾斯的部族聯軍在一名出身微賤、曾為羅馬軍人的領袖帶領下起事，避開兩支主力軍團，席捲泰恩河谷與斯坦蓋特防線上的邊境堡壘；帝國派禁軍護衛長率大軍入援，叛軍才於133年敗於談判。卡面的科林斯青銅盔屬古希臘閉面盔系，並未出現在北不列顛的戰場上。

kit.name: 科林斯青銅盔
kit.history: 全正面開眼的青銅盔。看得見的代價是：戴它的人只能靠隊形活。

countries: 公元132年爆發的這場衝突發生在羅馬不列顛行省境內，性質並非國家之間的戰爭，而是帝國邊疆的一次行省起事及其鎮壓。叛亂方是北不列顛與威爾斯地區的部族聯軍，主力來自泰恩河以北的布立吞人、康諾維人，以及中部與西南部的多布恩尼人、科里耶爾陶維人與奧爾維利人等部族的武裝隊伍；他們由一名被後世稱為「巴柯巴」的領袖率領，以部落兵團的形式投入戰鬥，隊伍之中還混有脫隊的羅馬軍人與被強行編入軍籍的輔助兵。值得留意的是，行省北部與威爾斯一帶的若干「客戶王」——在羅馬宗主權下保有王位、按約提供兵役的部族領袖——在起義中站在羅馬一方，可見叛亂並未得到全島的一致響應，起義的地理重心落在北部邊防地帶。鎮壓方是羅馬帝國：駐不列顛的兩支軍團——第二奧古斯塔軍團與第二十瓦勒里亞·維克特利克斯軍團——以及前沿各堡的輔助軍，即以步兵大隊為主、輔以騎兵大隊的常備部隊，構成本次平叛的骨幹；帝國中央另派禁軍護衛長朱利烏斯·阿斯克勒庇俄圖斯赴前線統籌，並由哈德良皇帝的親屬盧普斯率主力部隊進逼。全程沒有第三國介入，也沒有形成跨海聯盟，這自始至終是帝國內部的一場平叛。
countriesEn: The conflict that broke out in 132 AD took place inside the Roman province of Britannia and was in nature not a war between states but a provincial rising and its suppression on the empire's frontier. The insurgents were a tribal league drawn from the north of Britain and from Wales, the main body made up of war bands of the Brigantes and the Cornovii north of the Tyne together with bands of the Dobunni, the Corieltauvi and the Orbienses in the Midlands and the south-west; they were led by a man later called 'Bacon', serving in tribal war-band form, and their ranks also included Romans who had run off from their units and auxiliaries who had been pressed into service. It is worth noting that several of the 'client kings' of the northern and Welsh districts, that is tribal rulers who held their crowns under Roman suzerainty and owed troops by treaty, sided with Rome during the rising, so the rebellion did not command the assent of the whole island: its geographical centre of gravity lay in the frontier zone of the north. The side that suppressed it was the Roman Empire: the two legions stationed in Britain, the Second Augusta and the Twentieth Valeria Victrix, together with the auxiliaries of the frontier forts, a standing force made up mainly of infantry cohorts with cavalry alae, formed the backbone of the campaign; the centre of the empire additionally sent the praetorian prefect Julius Asclepiodotus to the front to coordinate operations, while Hadrian's relative Lupus brought up the main body of troops. No third country was involved at any point and no alliance was formed across the sea; from beginning to end this was a suppression of a revolt within the empire.
people: 這場起義留下的人名極少，而留下名字最多的偏偏是敵方。叛軍首領的姓名在原始記載中並不存在：狄奧·卡西烏斯只說這名領袖出身微賤，從前在羅馬軍中服役，後來脫隊，並且是被部眾以王號擁立者；今日通用的「巴柯巴」（Bacon）之名，是後世從訛傳的字形推演出來的，十八、十九世紀古物研究者的論著把它當作實名寫入史書，直到二十世紀的英國史家重新校讀狄奧原文，才確認原始記載並無此名。可能的實情是：這位領袖原是某位客戶王或部族首領，被叛軍加上了王號；也有說法認為他是一位被廢黜的客戶王。哈德良皇帝是全局的決策者，起義爆發時他不在軍中，卻迅速調動禁軍與輔助部隊赴英，並在前線主將之間作出取捨。禁軍護衛長朱利烏斯·阿斯克勒庇俄圖斯是此役最具決定性的人物，狄奧記載他沒有立刻求戰，而是先收攏四散的部隊、重新操練，再以密集方陣進攻，最後代表羅馬與叛軍首領談判達成協議。盧普斯（Lupus）是哈德良的親屬，率領主力推進，被認為是壓制叛軍的軍事骨幹；作戰期間的行省總督姓名在記錄中不詳，哈德良在平亂後改派盧利烏斯·烏爾比庫斯（Quintus Lollius Urbicus）出任不列顛總督，由他把防線改為泰恩至索爾韋灣的石牆線。第二奧古斯塔軍團的指揮官同樣沒有留下姓名，但他的軍團在平亂後駐紮約克，參與了後續的築牆工程。叛軍方面除首領外並無可考的將領姓名，起義的推動依賴各部族首領與地方望族，其中有人響應、有人觀望、有人站在羅馬一方；一位身份明確的地方人物是北部的客戶王，他以羅馬附庸的身分出兵，因而保住了自己的領地。
peopleEn: Very few personal names survive from this rising, and the ones that do belong mostly to the enemy side. The name of the insurgent leader does not exist in the original record: Cassius Dio says only that the man was of humble origin, had served in the Roman army, had deserted from it, and was acclaimed as a king by his followers; the name 'Bacon' now in use was reconstructed by later writers from corrupted forms, and was written into history as a proper name by antiquarians of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, until scholars in the twentieth century re-read Dio's text and confirmed that the original record contains no such name. The likeliest reconstruction is that the man was originally a client king or a tribal chief to whom the insurgents added a royal title; another view holds that he was a deposed client king. The emperor Hadrian was the decision maker for the whole affair: he was not in the field when the rising began, yet he moved the praetorian guard and auxiliary troops to Britain quickly and chose between his field commanders. The praetorian prefect Julius Asclepiodotus was the most decisive figure of the campaign; Dio records that he did not seek battle at once but first gathered up the scattered detachments, drilled them again, advanced in a solid phalanx, and finally negotiated a settlement on behalf of Rome with the insurgent leader. Lupus, a relative of Hadrian, brought up the main body of troops and is taken to have been the military weight that broke the revolt; the name of the provincial governor during the operations is not recorded, and after the suppression Hadrian replaced him with Quintus Lollius Urbicus as governor of Britain, the man who turned the frontier into the stone line from the Tyne to the Solway. The commander of the Second Augusta likewise left no name, but his legion stood at York after the suppression and took part in the wall works that followed. On the insurgent side there is no recoverable name for a commander: the movement was carried by tribal chiefs and local notables, some of whom answered the call, some watched, and some stood with Rome; one local figure of clear identity was the client king of the north, who campaigned as a Roman subordinate and in that way kept his own territory.
kits: 卡面是「科林斯青銅盔」：約公元前650年前後的希臘古式全封閉青銅盔，只留兩道眼縫與一道鼻脊，腦後收成尖錐，兩側垂下護頰；這類閉面盔在西元前六世紀已經是舊式，到古典時代被露臉的科林斯式與雅典式取代，公元132年的不列顛戰場上不可能出現這頂盔。把它放進這場戰爭，是要標示一條技術譜系：頭盔要在擋開正面打擊與讓戴盔者看清戰場之間取捨。閉面盔給了全頭防護，代價是視野只剩一線，戴盔者一旦離開隊列幾乎就是瞎子；而公元132年羅馬軍人頭上戴的是帝國高盧式頭盔，銅質、露臉、有前額護片與頸甲，輔助軍的銅盔常帶頂飾座，更晚的軍人又換上分片式護頭。線索的交點在狄奧的記載：朱利烏斯·阿斯克勒庇俄圖斯把部隊操練成密集方陣，列陣前進，長矛如林，盾牌相接——希臘重裝方陣的操典，正是這支部隊用來對付不列顛人的手法。裝備上，羅馬步兵以重型標槍（pilum，約二點二公尺長杆配鐵鏃）、長矛（hasta）、短劍（gladius）與匕首（pugio）為主，軍團士卒用半圓曲盾（scutum），輔助軍多用橢圓盾或小圓盾，護身有鎖子甲（lorica hamata）與分片甲（lorica segmentata），鞋為釘底皮靴（caligae）；騎兵大隊用流線長矛（contarius）、卡塔拉利式馬具與圓盾，輔助步兵還配可置於盾後的短刺標槍（plumbata），弓手與石弩手用於壓制牆頭與守城之敵。攻城與築城器材包括投石機、弩砲、撞柱與雲梯，牆體施工用到鐵鎬、石斧、灰泥與吊籃；羅馬在牆上按「里」設堡，每堡間隔約一點四八公里的羅馬里，牆後是連接各堡的軍用道路。不列顛叛軍的裝備主要來自本地鐵匠：帶柄長矛、短劍、投槍、柳條與木製小圓盾，另有少量舊式青銅盔與皮甲；他們沒有攻城器，攻堡靠火攻與人海，糧食靠劫掠莊園與村鎮。補給方面，羅馬主力由海路自高盧北上，經博洛尼亞、桑特港一帶登陸，抵達泰恩河口與索爾韋灣，再用馱馬與車隊沿軍用道路向前線運糧。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Corinthian helmet: an archaic Greek fully enclosed bronze helmet of about 650 BC, with only two eye slits and a nasal, the skull tapering to a point at the back and cheek pieces hanging at the sides. Closed helmets of this kind were already old-fashioned by the sixth century BC and were displaced in the classical age by the open-faced Corinthian and Attic types, so such a helmet cannot have been present on a battlefield in Britain in 132 AD. It is placed in this war to mark a line of technical descent: a helmet has to strike a balance between turning aside blows from the front and letting the wearer see the field. The closed face gave complete frontal protection at the price of a slit of vision, and once the wearer left the ranks he was very nearly blind; the Roman soldier of 132 AD, by contrast, wore the Imperial Gallic helmet in bronze, open-faced, with a brow guard and a neck guard, while auxiliary helmets were often bronze with a crest holder, and later men went over to segmented head protection. The point where the two threads meet is in Dio's account: Julius Asclepiodotus drilled his troops into a solid phalanx, advancing in close order with the long spears levelled like a forest and the shields touching, and the drill of the Greek armoured phalanx is precisely the hand that was used against the Britons. In terms of equipment, Roman infantry fought with the heavy pilum, a shaft of about two point two metres with an iron shank, the hasta, the gladius and the pugio; legionary men carried the semi-cylindrical scutum while auxiliaries used oval or small round shields, with lorica hamata and later lorica segmentata for the body and caligae with hobnails on the feet. Cavalry alae carried the contarius, a streaming lance, with cataphract-style harness and a round shield, and auxiliary infantry had the plumbata, a short weighted javelin that could be thrust over the shoulder of the shield, while archers and stone-throwers were used against men on walls and in defences. Siege and building equipment included ballistae, onagers, battering rams and scaling ladders, and the construction of the wall called for picks, stone axes, mortar and lifting baskets. The Romans laid out the wall by the Roman mile, about one point four eight kilometres from fort to fort, with a military way running behind it. The equipment of the British insurgents came mainly from local smiths: socketed spears, short swords, javelins, wicker and wooden small round shields, with a few old bronze helmets and leather armour. They had no siege train, took forts with fire and numbers, and lived off what they could seize from estates and villages. On the logistics side the Roman main body came north by sea from Gaul, landing around Boulogne and the ports of the Channel, reaching the mouth of the Tyne and the Solway, and then moved grain forward by pack-horse and cart along the military way.
tactics: 起義的開局戰術由狄奧寫得很清楚：不列顛人刻意避開兩支主力軍團，轉而攻擊散在鄉間的輔助軍小分隊、孤立堡壘與糧秣隊；可依仗的地形是森林、沼澤與丘陵交錯的北部，羅馬騎兵難以追擊，敵軍又慣於夜間行軍、白晝退入林地。史料與考古都顯示，這次攻勢以火為主：科布里奇的軍用堡壘在公元132年前後被焚毀，維多蘭達一帶也出現與130年代相符的燒毀層，堡壘的木構頂蓋與鋪地都留下火燒痕跡。叛軍的另一個目標是切斷前線與後方的聯繫：北方糧道沿斯坦蓋特驛道由科布里奇通往卡萊爾，道路與驛站是重點襲擊對象；客戶王與小部族被脅迫或被爭取，叛軍想用這一帶的人力與地勢把羅馬的北方堡壘群孤立。羅馬的反制分三步。第一步是不急於決戰：朱利烏斯·阿斯克勒庇俄圖斯把四散的分隊收攏，避開叛軍的鋒頭，優先重整兵種與指揮，據狄奧所記，他甚至退到有利的地形上等待。第二步是重塑陣形：他要求部隊結成密集方陣前進，把長矛持成如林的樣子，盾牌彼此相接，腳步齊整，並反覆操練在遭到衝擊時如何站穩腳跟、又如何以短兵接戰；同時以禁軍護衛的偵察騎保持與各堡的聯絡，使孤立的哨位不再被各個擊破。第三步是兵力對比：主力軍團自高盧渡海抵達後，叛軍再也無法只靠襲擊牽制，戰局很快傾斜。收官是政治解決：據狄奧，叛軍首領被說服，率殘部有條件投降，交還所占的堡壘與土地，羅馬方面則許以安全、寬待被俘者，並刻意把這份寬大寫進官方敘述，用以對比叛軍對羅馬俘虜的殘酷。戰後的防務改組是戰術層面的另一半：斯坦蓋特一線的堡壘被放棄，防線退到泰恩至索爾韋灣，石牆、里堡、望樓與外壕組成新的體系，牆後的軍用道路與固定的駐防輪替取代了過去季節性的巡邏。
tacticsEn: The opening tactics of the rising are set down clearly by Dio: the Britons deliberately avoided the two legions and turned instead on the small detachments of auxiliaries scattered in the countryside, on isolated forts and on supply columns. The ground they could rely on was the northern belt of forest, marsh and hill, where Roman cavalry could not pursue them, and they were accustomed to march by night and to withdraw into the woods by day. Both the narrative and the archaeology show that fire was the main instrument of this offensive: the military fort at Corbridge was burned down around 132 AD, and a destruction horizon matching the 130s has been found at Vindolanda, with scorch marks on the wooden roofs and on the beaten floors of the barrack blocks. The other aim of the insurgents was to cut the front from the rear: the northern supply road ran along the Stanegate from Corbridge towards Carlisle, and the road with its posting stations was the priority target for attack. Client kings and minor tribes were coerced or won over, for the insurgents wanted to use the manpower and the ground of that district to isolate the chain of Roman forts in the north. The Roman counter had three stages. The first was to refuse a premature battle: Asclepiodotus gathered in the scattered detachments, kept clear of the insurgent thrust, and put right the arms and the command before anything else, and Dio records that he even withdrew to favourable ground to wait. The second was to rebuild the formation: he required the troops to advance in a solid phalanx, to level the long spears like a forest, to keep the shields touching one another, to march in step, and he drilled them again and again in how to hold their footing when charged and how to close at short range, while the scouts of the praetorian guard kept contact with the forts so that isolated posts would no longer be taken one by one. The third was the balance of numbers: once the main body of the legions had crossed from Gaul, the insurgents could no longer live on the tactic of harassment alone and the course of the war tilted quickly. The closing stage was a political solution: according to Dio the insurgent leader was persuaded and surrendered the remnants on terms, handing back the forts and land he had taken, while Rome guaranteed his safety, treated the prisoners with clemency and deliberately put that clemency into the official narrative, to set it against the brutality the insurgents had shown to Roman prisoners. The reorganisation of the frontier after the war is the other half of the tactical story: the forts of the Stanegate line were abandoned, the frontier fell back to the Tyne and the Solway, and the stone wall with its mile-forts, watchtowers and outer ditch formed a new system, the military way behind the wall and fixed garrison rotations replacing the seasonal patrols of the past.
data: 可用的數字有限，以下幾組最為可靠。時間上，起事在公元132年爆發，戰事延續到133年被平定，前後約兩年，落在皇帝哈德良在位的中段，也正與哈德良城牆工程全面鋪開的時期重合。防線的長度可量：石牆自泰恩河口的塞格杜努姆至索爾韋灣的班納，橫越約一百二十公里；牆上按羅馬里設置堡壘，每座里堡相隔約一點四八公里，另築望樓與壕溝，牆後的軍用道路連接全線。羅馬在英軍力方面：公元132年的不列顛常備兩支軍團，即第二奧古斯塔與第二十瓦勒里亞·維克特利克斯，帝制時期單一軍團步兵通常在五千上下，兩團合計約一萬人；輔助軍在英國的駐防單位通常被估為四十支上下，含數支騎兵大隊（每隊約五百至七百五十人，千人隊約一千人）與數十支步兵大隊（每隊約四百八十至一千人），輔助兵總數多被估在一萬五千至兩萬之間；此外還有自羅馬遠派來的禁軍護衛分遣隊與偵察騎。叛軍的兵力沒有留下可核實的數字，古代作者只說起事席捲了北部的多個部族，近代學者多據各部族同時起兵的規模推測為數萬人，但這一數字只能視為量級而非確數。距離與時間：科布里奇至卡萊爾的斯坦蓋特驛道約一百公里，一支羅馬縱隊沿線行軍需時數日；叛軍襲擊分散哨所可以一兩日之內完成，羅馬重新集結主力並操練密集方陣所花的時間以月計。考古斷代方面，科布里奇堡壘的焚毀層被定在公元130年代，維多蘭達的毀壞層以碳十四定在公元125至140年之間，兩者都與132年前後的動亂相容。雙方死傷數字，史料完全沒有記載，近代估算彼此矛盾，本檔不採用任何一方提出的傷亡總數。產能方面，牆體用石量、灰泥與木材的消耗古代沒有留下可核的統計；同期埋藏的銅錢窖藏，則與戰亂時期現金流通中斷的情形相合。
dataEn: Only a limited number of figures are available, and the following groups are the most reliable. In time, the rising broke out in 132 AD and was not settled until 133, roughly two years in all, falling in the middle of the reign of Hadrian and coinciding with the phase in which the works on Hadrian's Wall were in full swing. The length of the frontier can be measured: the stone wall runs from Segedunum at the mouth of the Tyne to Banna on the Solway Firth, a crossing of about one hundred and twenty kilometres; mile-forts were set out by the Roman mile along it, about one point four eight kilometres apart, with watchtowers and ditches besides, and a military way running behind the wall to link the whole line. On the strength of Rome in Britain in 132: two legions were permanently stationed there, the Second Augusta and the Twentieth Valeria Victrix; under the empire a single legion normally held about five thousand foot, so the two together came to roughly ten thousand men. The auxiliary garrison in Britain is usually reckoned at about forty units, including a number of cavalry alae of five hundred to seven hundred and fifty men each, a milliaria of about a thousand, and several dozen infantry cohorts of about four hundred and eighty to a thousand men each, so that the auxiliary total is commonly estimated at between fifteen and twenty thousand; on top of this came a detachment of the praetorian guard sent from the city of Rome together with its scouts. The strength of the insurgents leaves no verifiable figure; the ancient writers say only that the rising swept through several tribes of the north, and modern scholars infer a force of tens of thousands from the fact that several tribes rose at once, but that number can only be treated as an order of magnitude and not as an exact count. Distance and time: the Stanegate road from Corbridge to Carlisle is about one hundred kilometres, and a Roman column marching along it took several days; the insurgents could strike a scattered detachment within a day or two, whereas the time Rome spent on concentrating the main body and on drilling the phalanx is measured in months. On archaeological dating, the burnt horizon of the fort at Corbridge has been placed in the 130s AD, and the destruction layer at Vindolanda has been radiocarbon dated to between 125 and 140 AD, both of which are compatible with the disturbances of around 132. On casualties the sources are completely silent, and the modern estimates contradict one another, so no total of losses is adopted here. On production, the ancient record leaves no verifiable statistics for the consumption of stone, mortar and timber in the wall, while the coin hoards buried at about the same time fit the picture of cash circulation breaking down during the fighting.
cause: 關於起事的原因，史料留下的是一條線索而不是一份清單，最終只能從羅馬在英國的治理結構反推。第一層是財政：公元132年的不列顛行省需要自行供給駐軍的糧秣、軍械與薪餉，省內稅收長期不足，帝國便向客戶王、向莊園與地方首領加派攤派，以「奉獻」名義徵收的錢財，在帝國的財政系統中等同於戰時稅。第二層是土地：哈德良城牆本身需要大量土地、磚石與人力，北部客戶王的土地被直接徵用，公路、堡壘與駐軍地帶切走了原有的牧場與耕地，地方權益在沒有補償或補償不足的情況下被剝奪。第三層是兵役與人力：帝國在英的兩支軍團與數十支輔助軍不斷由高盧、高盧南部與東方補充兵員，客戶王必須按約提供軍團作戰單位，地方青壯被徵召，邊境的屯田與工程勞役都被攤到部族頭上。第四層是帝國的姿態：哈德良即位後放棄了此前的征服政策，改以固定線界與防衛網取代深入腹地的戰役，這一轉向本身就意味著北部的軍力密度與控制強度上升。需要交代的是，長期流傳的「蠻族反攻羅馬、哈德良城牆逼出起義」說法，在今天的學界已讓位於財政、土地與兵役的解釋；不少研究者反過來認為，石牆在132年之後才移到現址，因此城牆與起義互為因果的那部分，方向可能與舊說相反。觸發點則難以確指：可以確定的是，起義爆發時前沿輔助軍已減員或調離、堡壘分散而空，而叛軍選擇了避開主力軍團、專打小分隊的辦法。地方首領之間對是否跟從的分歧，起義能擴散到多個部族的原因，也在此列。
causeEn: On the causes of the rising, the record leaves a clue rather than a list, and they can only be worked out backwards from the way Rome governed Britain. The first layer is finance: the province of Britannia in 132 AD had to supply the grain, the arms and the pay of the garrison from its own resources, and provincial revenue was chronically short, so the empire loaded the client kings, the estates and the local notables with additional levies, and money demanded under the name of a 'donation' was in the imperial financial system simply a war tax. The second layer is land: Hadrian's Wall itself demanded a great deal of land, stone and labour, the lands of the northern client kings were taken for it outright, and the roads, forts and garrison zones cut into existing pasture and arable, so local rights were stripped away without compensation or with too little of it. The third layer is service and man-power: the two legions in Britain and the several dozen auxiliary units were continuously replenished from Gaul, from southern Gaul and from the east, the client kings were bound by treaty to furnish contingents for the legions, and the young men of the districts were conscripted, with frontier settlement works and the labour of the wall falling on the tribes. The fourth layer is the posture of the empire: after his accession Hadrian gave up the policy of conquest in favour of a fixed line and a network of defence in place of campaigns deep into the interior, and that turn itself meant higher troop density and firmer control in the north. It should be said that the long-standing story of a barbarian rising against Rome, with Hadrian's Wall as the spark, has given way in current scholarship to an explanation built on finance, land and service; a number of researchers argue the other way round, that the wall only moved to its present line after 132, so on the part of the record where wall and revolt are cause and effect of one another, the direction of causation may be the reverse of the old account. The trigger itself is hard to fix: what can be established is that the auxiliary troops on the frontier had been reduced or withdrawn when the rising broke out, that the forts were scattered and thin, and that the insurgents chose to avoid the legions and to strike small detachments. The disagreement among local notables over whether to follow also belongs in this list, for it explains how the rising spread across several tribes.
impact: 這場起義對不列顛的邊防格局有長期而具體的後果。它最直接的結果，是羅馬放棄了深入北方的推進計畫：斯坦蓋特一線的堡壘群被放棄，北方最外側的兩處前哨——哈比特安庫姆（羅辛厄姆）與布雷門尼烏姆（羅徹斯特高地）——隨後被撤除，羅馬的勢力自此不再越過泰恩至索爾韋灣這條線；其後安敦寧皇帝與塞維魯皇帝兩度把防線推到更北的堡壘線，每一次都以放棄新線、退回哈德良城牆收場。城牆於是從「工程」變成「制度」：堡壘、望樓、壕溝、軍用道路與固定的駐防輪替被寫成常態的邊防體系，兩支軍團分別駐紮約克與切斯特，輔助軍填滿牆上各堡，後方供應線由船隊與陸路車隊維持。第三，它在考古上留下可見的痕跡：公元130年代的燒毀層、被掩埋的路面、匆忙填平或改建後的營房，說明衝突不是一場幾天的插曲，而是對邊防設施的實體破壞。第四，它改寫了學界與公眾對這段歷史的敘述。十八、十九世紀的作家把「巴柯巴」寫成一位明確的國王與抵抗象徵，後來的民族文學也曾借用這場起義；二十世紀的史家重新核對狄奧的原文與考古材料之後，指出原始記載並無此名，起義的規模、領導結構與羅馬的應對方式都與後世想像有相當差距，這場戰爭於是從民族英雄的敘事被拉回「帝國邊疆治理與財政成本」的層面。第五，它把一段被忽略的技術史推到前台：古希臘的閉面青銅盔早已退場，羅馬軍人戴的是露臉的帝國高盧盔，決定戰鬥勝負的卻是隊形——密集方陣、盾牌相接、標槍如林，這是希臘重裝步兵的操典，被帝國借來對付不列顛部族的襲擊。武器史在此不靠更精巧的盔，而靠在把裝備與陣形綁在一起。
impactEn: The rising had long-term and very concrete consequences for the military geography of Britain. Its most direct result was that Rome abandoned the plan of pushing deep into the north: the chain of forts on the Stanegate line was given up, and the two outermost posts in the north, Habitancum at Risingham and Bremenium at High Rochester, were subsequently withdrawn, so that Roman power no longer crossed the line from the Tyne to the Solway, apart from the two later moves north under Antoninus Pius and Septimius Severus, each of which ended with the new line abandoned and the army falling back to Hadrian's Wall. The wall thus changed from a work into an institution: forts, watchtowers, ditches, military ways and fixed garrison rotations were written into a permanent frontier system, the two legions sat at York and at Chester, the auxiliaries filled the forts along the line, and the supply line behind was kept up by the fleets and by wagon trains on the roads. Third, it left visible traces in the archaeology: the burnt horizons of the 130s, levelled road surfaces, barracks hastily filled in or rebuilt, all showing that the conflict was no brief episode but a real destruction of the frontier works. Fourth, it rewrote the story told about this period by scholars and by the public. Writers of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries set 'Bacon' down as a definite king and a symbol of resistance, and later national literature borrowed the rising for its own purposes; when twentieth-century historians went back over Dio's text and the archaeological material, they found that the original record contains no such name and that the scale of the revolt, its leadership structure and the Roman response differ considerably from the later imagining, and the war was moved back from the register of national heroism to that of imperial frontier administration and fiscal cost. Fifth, it pushed a neglected strand of technical history into the light: the closed bronze helmet of archaic Greece had long since retired, the Roman soldier wore the open-faced Imperial Gallic helm, and what decided the fighting was the formation, the solid phalanx, the touching shields, the levelled pila, an inheritance from the armoured infantry of Greece borrowed by the empire to meet the raids of the British tribes. Here the history of weapons is not a matter of a cleverer helmet but of binding the equipment to the formation.
result: 公元133年，叛亂平定。據狄奧記載，叛軍首領被說服，以有條件的方式交出殘部與所占的堡壘，羅馬方面接受投降，保證其安全並寬待被俘者；作為交換，被叛軍攻陷的堡壘與土地回到羅馬手中。哈德良隨即改組不列顛的指揮與防務：撤換行省總督，任命盧利烏斯·烏爾比庫斯接掌，把石牆移到泰恩至索爾韋灣的現址，動用第二奧古斯塔與第二十瓦勒里亞·維克特利克斯兩軍團及各輔助大隊築牆、設堡、鋪路，並放棄北方的哈比特安庫姆與布雷門尼烏姆兩處前哨。叛軍方面沒有取得任何國家承認，沒有一份條約留下名字，首領在記載中自此消失，餘部被解為奴隸或被強制編入軍隊、發往行省各地；留在原位的客戶王則得到確認，作為附庸繼續提供軍團與兵役。從帝國的角度看，這場戰爭的代價是幾個月的兵役、數處邊防堡壘被焚毀，以及一批再也回不來的守軍，而換來的是一條固定下來的邊界：以石牆、堡壘與常備軍取代此前的進攻與遠征。從不列顛部族的角度看，起義沒有換來自治或土地，只換來更密的帝國駐軍與更重的徵發；但它確實迫使羅馬放棄了向北深入的計畫，改以一條線把北境圈在牆外。軍事史上，這場戰爭留下兩處常被引用的細節：狄奧記錄的密集方陣操練，說明以希臘方陣基因解決衝鋒是一條可行的技術路線；而那頂卡面的古希臘閉面青銅盔，恰好說明了一件更根本的事：當視野只剩一線的時候，人就只能靠隊形活著離開戰場。
resultEn: In 133 AD the rebellion was settled. According to Dio, the insurgent leader was persuaded and handed over the remnants and the forts he had taken on terms; Rome accepted the surrender, guaranteed his safety and treated the prisoners with clemency, and in exchange the forts and land seized by the insurgents came back into Roman hands. Hadrian then reorganised the command and the frontier of Britain: the provincial governor was replaced and Quintus Lollius Urbicus was appointed in his place, the stone wall was moved to its present line from the Tyne to the Solway, the Second Augusta and the Twentieth Valeria Victrix with the auxiliary units were set to building the wall, laying out the forts and paving the roads, and the two outermost posts in the north, Habitancum and Bremenium, were abandoned. The insurgents gained no recognition from any state, no treaty preserves their name, the leader disappears from the record after this, and the remnants were sold into slavery or forced into the army and sent out to the provinces; the client kings who stayed in place were confirmed and continued to furnish troops and service as subordinates. From the point of view of the empire, the price of the war was some months of service, several frontier forts burned down and a body of soldiers who would never come back, and what it bought was a frontier fixed in place: a stone wall, forts and a standing army in place of the campaigns and expeditions of before. From the point of view of the British tribes, the rising brought neither autonomy nor land, only denser Roman garrisons and heavier levies; but it did force Rome to give up the plan of advancing deep into the north and to enclose the northern frontier beyond a single line. In military history the war left two details that are often quoted: the drill in a solid phalanx recorded by Dio, which shows that answering the charge with the formation inherited from Greece was a workable technical solution; and the closed bronze helmet of archaic Greece on the card, which makes a more fundamental point: when the field of view is reduced to a slit, a man can only leave the field of battle alive by means of his formation.
